alternative.title: Cape May's 'World's Largest' Claims
alternative.description: Small American towns frequently compete for quirky 'world's largest' titles — from the world's largest ball of twine (Kansas) to the world's largest catsup bottle (Illinois) — a staple of American roadside culture.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of a 'world's largest' roadside attraction

alternative.title: Walt Disney World Opens in Florida
alternative.description: Disney's second American theme park opened near Orlando in 1971 on land quietly purchased under shell companies to avoid inflating prices before the project was announced.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of Walt Disney World's opening, 1971

alternative.title: The Great Molasses Flood's Lingering Legend
alternative.description: Locals in Boston's North End long claimed that on hot summer days, the neighborhood still smelled faintly of molasses decades after the 1919 flood.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of Boston's North End neighborhood

alternative.title: The 'Twinkie Defense'
alternative.description: During the 1979 trial for the assassination of San Francisco officials, a psychiatric defense citing the defendant's junk-food-heavy diet was nicknamed the 'Twinkie defense' by the press.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of a Twinkie snack cake

alternative.title: The Emu War... Wasn't American
alternative.description: Often confused with Australia's 1932 'Emu War,' the U.S. has its own share of odd wildlife skirmishes, including officially declared 'nuisance' campaigns against invasive species like nutria and Asian carp.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of wildlife management efforts

alternative.title: Cleveland's Balloonfest Disaster
alternative.description: A charity balloon release of 1.5 million balloons in Cleveland went awry when a storm blew them back over the city, grounding air and boat traffic and hampering a search for missing boaters.
alternative.mediaLabel: Photograph of Cleveland's 1986 Balloonfest release

alternative.title: Vermont's Real Maple Syrup Rules
alternative.description: Vermont maintains strict state grading laws for maple syrup, and it's illegal in the state to sell syrup labeled 'Vermont maple syrup' unless it was made entirely within Vermont.
